Transparency & control

Editorial standards & AI transparency

Read the evidence. Understand the uncertainty. Report mistakes.

What the app does

TruthLens India aggregates news and public information, generates AI-assisted claim analysis and tracks longer-running crises. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Government of India. Government sources, where cited, are source material and do not imply official status.

AI limitations

Summaries, analysis, verdicts and confidence scores may be produced automatically. They can be incomplete or wrong. A numerical score is a model assessment, not a calibrated probability or guarantee. Unless an item explicitly identifies a human reviewer, do not assume it was reviewed by an expert. Unverified claims are not established facts.

Sources and attribution

Each published news item should identify its original publisher or author and link to supporting sources. We distinguish original reporting from our analysis. Sources can disagree or change; readers should inspect the originals and their dates. We do not claim ownership of linked reporting. Licensing and permission requirements apply even when attribution is given.

Corrections and content standards

We investigate reports of errors, fabricated sources, harmful content and copyright issues. We may correct, label, restrict or remove an item. We aim to avoid misleading headlines, unsupported accusations and presentation of automated analysis as established fact. Contact begoneraj@gmail.com with the article ID and supporting evidence.

Ownership and independence

The publisher is Pushpraj singh prashant. This release contains no advertising or paid subscriptions. No professional accreditation, award or government endorsement is claimed.
